projectDesc.p: The dataset records verified sources of unacknowledged quotation, adaptation, echo and allusion in Prynne's Poems (2005) and Force of Circumstance (1962). A source is recorded only where its own words were seen in the edition named. Sources were found by close reading (agents working to a written brief, then an adversarial verifier, then the author's review) and by two deterministic sweeps: four-word phrase searches of the Internet Archive's full text, limited to texts dated no later than the collection, and an n-gram match against Project Gutenberg. Pages 556-576 of Poems (including the whole of Blue Slides At Rest) and its index were transcribed from a second scan of the same edition.

editorialDecl.p: Prynne's page and line. Pages are those of the editions in the sourceDesc. Lines follow literary convention: they are the lines of the poem, counted from its first line. Titles, epigraphs and dedications are not counted; a reference to one of them is a citedRange with unit title, epigraph or dedication. A verse line turned over onto a second typographic line counts as one line. The lines of a poem are counted on across its pages and its numbered sections. An untitled poem in a sequence is a poem as the book's index of first lines gives it, and its title in the dataset is that first line. The corresp of each Prynne quote points to the xml:id of its first typographic line (p302.14: page 302, fourteenth printed line) in the private transcription, which is not published.

Quotation. Each quote holds only the words that the two passages share: the runs of consecutive words of one passage that all occur in the other, with runs of a single common function word dropped. Breaks between runs are gap reason="omitted"; a line break in Prynne is lb. An entry with no shared words (an allusion) has no quote.

Editions. Each source bibl points to the edition in which its words were seen. Identifiers (idno) were resolved from Crossref, the Library of Congress, Open Library, the Internet Archive and Wikidata, and each was matched to the author, title and date before it was recorded. A field is left empty rather than guessed. The date of the work, where it differs from the edition's, is in a relatedItem type="original".
Confidence (cert) is the verifier's judgement that the passage draws on the source: high, medium or low.
